title: Parts of a circle
keyIdea: Every point on a circle's edge is the same distance from its centre. That distance is the radius, and a line from the centre to the edge is also called a radius. A diameter is a straight line from edge to edge through the centre, so it is made of two radii: diameter = 2 × radius. The circumference is the distance all the way round the edge, a bit more than 3 diameters. Compasses draw a circle with the opening set to the radius.
familyTip: Find something round at home: a plate, a lid or a coin. Ask your child to point to the centre, trace the circumference with a finger and lay a pencil across as a diameter. Wrap a string round a tin, then see how many times the tin's width fits along the string.

visual.caption: Which part of a circle is it? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: Edge to edge through the centre
All the way round the edge
A bit more than 3 diameters long

lab.caption: Flagship lab: name the parts, turn a radius, make a diameter, set compasses, roll a wheel one turn, check a robot.

kid: A circle has one point in the middle, called the centre. Every point on the edge is the same distance from the centre. That is what makes it round.
A straight line from the centre to the edge is a radius. Turn it any way you like and it stays the same length. Two or more are called radii.
A diameter is a straight line from edge to edge that passes through the centre. It is made of two radii end to end, so it is twice as long as the radius. If the radius is 4 cm, the diameter is 8 cm.
The circumference is the curved edge, and its length is the distance all the way round. Roll a wheel one full turn and it moves a bit more than 3 times its diameter.
adult: Ages 10 to 11. In England's Year 6 maths, children illustrate and name parts of circles, including radius, diameter and circumference, and know that the diameter is twice the radius. Key words: centre, radius, radii, diameter, circumference, chord, compasses.

The radius is both a length and a line segment from the centre to the circumference. The diameter is a chord through the centre and the longest chord of the circle, so d = 2r and r = d ÷ 2. Compasses keep the point on the centre and the pencil at the radius, which is why the opening is the radius.

A common mistake is to call any line across a circle a diameter: it must pass through the centre, or it is a shorter chord. Children also mix up which way to convert, halving the radius to get the diameter. Another slip is to set compasses to the diameter, which draws a circle twice as wide. Some think the circumference means the width.

In the lab your child names each part with a decoy chord, turns a radius to three places and sees it stay 4 cm, drags a point until a line becomes a diameter, opens compasses to the radius, and rolls wheels one turn to see the circumference is a bit more than 3 diameters. The exact rule with pi comes in the next topic.

practice.prompt: A circle has a radius of {a} cm. How long is its diameter, in cm?
practice.hint: A diameter is two radii end to end through the centre.

practice.prompt: A round table is {=2*a} cm across through its centre. What is its radius, in cm?
practice.hint: The distance across through the centre is the diameter. The radius is half of it.

practice.prompt: A straight line joins two points on a circle but does not pass through the centre. What is it called?
practice.hint: A diameter must go through the centre, and a radius must start at the centre.
practice.explain: It is a chord. Only the chord that passes through the centre is a diameter, and it is the longest chord.

practice.prompt: You want to draw a circle 10 cm across. How wide should you open the compasses?
practice.hint: The point of the compasses sits on the centre and the pencil traces the edge.
practice.explain: 10 cm across is the diameter. The compass opening is the radius, half of 10 cm, so open them to 5 cm.

practice.prompt: Which is the circumference of a bicycle wheel?
choices: The length of the tyre all the way round
The length of one spoke from the hub to the rim
The distance across the wheel through the hub
practice.hint: Circumference is about going round the curved edge.
practice.explain: The circumference is the distance all the way round the edge, the tyre. A spoke is like a radius, and the distance across through the hub is the diameter.

pool.prompt: The radius of a coin is {a} mm. What is its diameter, in mm?
pool.hint: Double the radius to get the diameter.

pool.prompt: The diameter of a pond is {=2*a} m. What is its radius, in m?
pool.hint: The radius is half the diameter.

pool.prompt: Which statement about one circle is true?
choices: All its radii are the same length
A radius pointing sideways is longer than one pointing up
Its diameter is half its radius
pool.hint: Think about what makes a circle round: every point on the edge is the same distance from the centre.
pool.explain: Every point on the edge is the same distance from the centre, so every radius has the same length, whichever way it points.

pool.prompt: Which line is the longest straight line you can draw inside a circle?
choices: A chord that misses the centre
pool.hint: Try moving one end of a line round the edge and watch its length.
pool.explain: A diameter passes through the centre and is the longest chord. Any chord that misses the centre is shorter, and a radius is only half a diameter.

pool.prompt: A wheel has a diameter of 50 cm. About how far does it roll in one full turn?
pool.hint: One full turn rolls out the circumference, which is a bit more than 3 diameters.
pool.explain: One turn rolls out the circumference, a bit more than 3 × 50 = 150 cm (about 157 cm).

pool.prompt: Sam says a line across a circle is a diameter. What must be true for Sam to be right?
choices: It is drawn with a ruler
It goes from left to right
pool.hint: A diameter is a special chord. What makes it special?
pool.explain: A diameter is a chord that passes through the centre. Its direction does not matter, but missing the centre makes it a shorter chord.

pool.prompt: Ali opens his compasses to 6 cm and draws a circle. How wide is the circle across the centre?
pool.hint: The compass opening is the radius of the circle it draws.
pool.explain: The opening, 6 cm, is the radius. The width through the centre is the diameter: 2 × 6 = 12 cm.

pool.prompt: Point O is the centre of a circle and P is a point on its circumference. What is the line from O to P?
pool.hint: Where does the line start, and where does it end?
pool.explain: It starts at the centre and ends on the edge, so OP is a radius. A diameter and a chord both join two points on the edge.
